sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Clicking the red dot also had no effect on the gameplay. Only the bottom bar (timer) decreases. In other words, clicking on the object body/dot does nothing.
Maybe the game requires clicking the red plus shape. Or perhaps it's a "click and drag" operation where a single MOUSE click just selects, and then a second click places it. Or maybe you need to click the container slot.
Let me try clicking the red plus at the top right (10,52) — the center is B (black), and the r pixels are around it. Actually, the center of the plus is (10,52) = B. Hmm, the plus is made of 4 r pixels around a black center. Clicking (10,52) might hit the black center.
Or maybe the plus is a "target marker" indicating where the object should be moved. The green block is at r9-11 c28-32, and the plus is at r9-11 c51-53 — same row! The yellow bar is at r28-35 c9-11, and the plus is at r51-53 c9-11 — same column! So the plus indicates the target position for each object: the green block should move to the plus position (rightward), and the yellow bar should move to the plus position (downward).
But how do you move them? Maybe click the object to select it, then click the destination. Or maybe click the plus to "pull" the object. Or maybe the object moves when you click it… but clicking the green block did nothing.
Wait — maybe the click needs to be on a specific part. The green block has a G cap on the left (c27), and the yellow bar has a G cap on top (r27). The red dot is on the green at (10,31), and on the yellow at (34,10). Hmm.
Maybe this is a "drag" game where MOUSE(row,col) means "drag to that position"? But the action is just a single click. Or maybe clicking the plus makes the nearest object move there?
Let me try clicking the center of the plus (10,52).
